bundles.title: Stage 1 · Rubber, stopping and shifting
bundles.summary: Wear items that are due anyway. The fastest and safest money on the bike.

bundles.title: Stage 2 · Wheels and visibility
bundles.summary: Lighter, stiffer alloy wheels with a wider rim, plus rear radar.

bundles.title: Climbing gears
bundles.summary: An 11–32 cassette with the medium-cage derailleur that supports it.

bundles.title: Power and data
bundles.summary: Measure the engine. Turns the estimates in this app into numbers.

bundles.title: Superteam 50 + GP5000 AS TR 28
bundles.summary: The wind-tunnel study: 50 mm carbon wheels on 28 mm all-season tyres, with the carbon pads they need and the Edge 1050.

components.name: Cannondale Synapse Carbon 51 · white/red
components.notes: Model year provisional: seller 2011; likely MY2012. Interfaces inferred from generation pending measurement. A 2012 listing names a "SAVE PLUS Multiflex" seatpost system, so read the post diameter off the part before buying one.

components.name: Fulcrum Racing · 622 × 15C alloy
components.mass_source: Racing 5 claim (later C17 generation); the installed 15C rim is older, so approximate
components.notes: Identified from photos: black rim with a white RACING band, ETRTO 622×15C aluminium. Read the model number on the rim (Racing 5 or 7).

components.name: Campagnolo Zonda C17 · alloy, HG freehub
components.mass_source: Manufacturer claim, pair (one retailer lists 1,540 g)
components.notes: Order the Shimano HG freehub version. On an 11-speed (HG-11) freehub a 10-speed cassette needs the 1.85 mm spacer.

upgrade.why: About 50 g lighter than the installed Racing with a stiffer rear wheel and a 17 mm internal rim that supports a 25 mm tyre properly. The long-standing benchmark alloy rim-brake wheel.

components.name: Fulcrum Racing 3 C17 · alloy
components.notes: On an 11-speed (HG-11) freehub a 10-speed cassette needs the 1.85 mm spacer.

upgrade.why: Sister wheel to the Zonda from the same factory, marketed for Shimano drivetrains. Choose on price and availability.

components.name: DT Swiss P 1800 Spline · alloy, tubeless-ready
components.notes: On an 11-speed (HG-11) freehub a 10-speed cassette needs the 1.85 mm spacer.

upgrade.why: Serviceable DT hub internals and a tubeless-ready rim. The durable, low-drama choice.

components.name: Hunt 4 Season Aero · alloy, 19 mm internal
components.notes: On an 11-speed (HG-11) freehub a 10-speed cassette needs the 1.85 mm spacer.

upgrade.why: Wide rim, extra spokes and sealed bearings for year-round riding. The 19 mm internal width makes a 25 mm tyre measure close to 27 mm, so check frame clearance first.

components.name: Superteam 50 mm carbon clincher · 700c, rim brake
components.mass_source: Listing for this ASIN, pair; other Superteam 50 mm listings claim 1,560 ± 30 g. Weigh on delivery (M16).
components.notes: Listings describe a 12-layer carbon brake track, so selecting it also fits carbon-specific pads; if the delivered set has an alloy track the installed pads stay. Reviews report heavier, more flexible wheels than branded carbon, bearing noise in rain and tubes pinched at the valve hole. On an 11-speed (HG-11) freehub a 10-speed cassette needs the 1.85 mm spacer.

perf.cda_basis: Wind-tunnel study in the Aero tab (cases with the _st28 suffix)

specs.spec_source: Amazon listing and retailer copies of it; CompleteTri review

upgrade.why: A 50 mm aero rim for a third of the price of a branded set. The tunnel study in the Aero tab measures what it is worth on this bike.

components.name: Hunt 50 Carbon Wide Aero · carbon brake track
components.notes: Carbon brake track: change to carbon-specific pads at the same time. On an 11-speed (HG-11) freehub a 10-speed cassette needs the 1.85 mm spacer.

upgrade.why: A true aero wheel. It needs carbon-specific pads, brakes worse in the wet, and its 27 mm outer width must clear the calipers and stays.

components.name: Vittoria Rubino Pro · 700 × 23
components.notes: Read from the sidewall: Rubino Pro 23-622. Inspect the rear sidewall damage noted in October.

perf.crr_basis: Rubino Pro III, 25 mm, 80 psi drum test (0.0048). Later G+ versions tested 0.0055–0.0057.

components.name: Continental Grand Prix 5000 · 700 × 25
components.mass_source: Bicycle Rolling Resistance measured 221 g each

requires.msg: Measured 26 mm wide on an 18 mm rim. Measure tyre clearance at the fork crown, calipers and chainstays (M15).

perf.crr_basis: Measured at 80 psi on a drum, 25 mm, butyl tube

upgrade.why: The largest gain per dollar on this bike. Rolling resistance drops by a third against a training tyre, grip improves, and it replaces a rear tyre with a damaged sidewall.

components.name: Continental GP5000 AS TR · 700 × 25 · black
components.mass_source: Bicycle Rolling Resistance measured 282 g each (claim 300 g), pair
components.price_source: Approximate Amazon price for a pair, 2026-11; verify

requires.msg: Measures 26 mm on an 18 mm rim. Measure clearance at the fork crown, calipers and chainstays (M15).

components.notes: Drum figures are tubeless; with a butyl tube the analysis adds 0.0006 to Crr.

perf.crr_basis: Drum test, 80 psi, tubeless with 20 ml sealant, 12.6 W per tyre at 29 km/h and 42.5 kg.

specs.spec_source: Bicycle Rolling Resistance (tested, tubeless) · Continental claims via retailers

upgrade.why: All-season GP5000: a Vectran belt bead to bead, the best wet grip in the range and a fifth less rolling resistance than the Rubino it replaces.

components.name: Continental GP5000 AS TR · 700 × 25 · black/cream
components.mass_source: Continental claim 305 g each (UK importer), pair; not weighed by BRR
components.price_source: Approximate Amazon price for a pair, 2026-11; verify

requires.msg: Measures 26 mm on an 18 mm rim. Measure clearance at the fork crown, calipers and chainstays (M15).

components.notes: Black/Cream skin. Drum figures are tubeless; with a butyl tube the analysis adds 0.0006 to Crr.

perf.crr_basis: Drum test, 80 psi, tubeless with 20 ml sealant, 12.6 W per tyre at 29 km/h and 42.5 kg; black/cream skin assumed equal to the tested black tyre.

specs.spec_source: Bicycle Rolling Resistance (tested, tubeless) · Continental claims via retailers

upgrade.why: All-season GP5000: a Vectran belt bead to bead, the best wet grip in the range and a fifth less rolling resistance than the Rubino it replaces.

components.name: Continental GP5000 AS TR · 700 × 28 · black
components.mass_source: Bicycle Rolling Resistance measured 345 g each (claim 335 g), pair
components.price_source: Approximate Amazon price for a pair, 2026-11; verify

requires.msg: Measures 29 mm on an 18 mm rim: at or beyond what rim-brake frames of this generation clear. Measure before buying (M15).
The selected calipers are not rated for a 28 mm tyre.

components.notes: Drum figures are tubeless; with a butyl tube the analysis adds 0.0006 to Crr.

perf.crr_basis: Drum test, 72 psi, tubeless with 20 ml sealant, 12.2 W per tyre at 29 km/h and 42.5 kg.

specs.spec_source: Bicycle Rolling Resistance (tested, tubeless) · Continental claims via retailers

upgrade.why: The comfort pick: lower pressure, more grip and slightly lower rolling resistance than the 25, if and only if the frame and calipers clear 29 mm.

components.name: Continental GP5000 AS TR · 700 × 28 · black/cream
components.mass_source: Continental claim 340 g each (UK importer), pair; not weighed by BRR
components.price_source: Approximate Amazon price for a pair, 2026-11; verify

requires.msg: Measures 29 mm on an 18 mm rim: at or beyond what rim-brake frames of this generation clear. Measure before buying (M15).
The selected calipers are not rated for a 28 mm tyre.

components.notes: Black/Cream skin. Drum figures are tubeless; with a butyl tube the analysis adds 0.0006 to Crr.

perf.crr_basis: Drum test, 72 psi, tubeless with 20 ml sealant, 12.2 W per tyre at 29 km/h and 42.5 kg; black/cream skin assumed equal to the tested black tyre.

specs.spec_source: Bicycle Rolling Resistance (tested, tubeless) · Continental claims via retailers

upgrade.why: The comfort pick: lower pressure, more grip and slightly lower rolling resistance than the 25, if and only if the frame and calipers clear 29 mm.

requires.msg: Measure safe tyre clearance (M15).

upgrade.why: Fast clincher available with a classic tan sidewall.

requires.msg: Measure safe tyre clearance (M15).

upgrade.why: Nylon-casing race tyre that tolerates rough roads. Tubeless-ready, usable with tubes on the current rims.

requires.msg: A 28 mm tyre is at or beyond what rim-brake frames of this generation usually clear. Do not buy before measuring (M15).
The selected calipers are not rated for a 28 mm tyre.

upgrade.why: More comfort and grip at lower pressure, if and only if the frame, fork and calipers clear it.

components.name: Installed inner tubes · assumed butyl
components.notes: Material and size unverified.

perf.crr_add_basis: Butyl tube vs tubeless on the same tyre: about 2 W per tyre at the BRR drum conditions (29 km/h, 42.5 kg), i.e. Crr +0.0006. Approximate.

components.name: TPU inner tubes (Tubolito / RideNow class)
components.notes: Use only models the maker rates for rim brakes: heat from long descents softens TPU. Pack one as the spare regardless.

upgrade.why: Saves roughly 130 g of rotating mass for the pair and rolls slightly faster than butyl. Also the smallest spare you can carry.

components.name: Latex inner tubes
components.notes: Lose pressure overnight, so pump before every ride. Not for carbon brake tracks.

upgrade.why: The lowest rolling resistance of any tube and a noticeably smoother ride, in exchange for daily inflation.

components.name: FSA Gossamer BB30 · 50/34 N10, 110 BCD
components.notes: Crank length to read (M10). Listings disagree on mass (751 g and 808 g), so no reference mass is used.

components.name: Cannondale HollowGram Si BB30 · 50/34
components.notes: Cannondale’s own BB30 crank; fits the existing bearings. Used-market price shown.

upgrade.why: Native BB30, hollow-forged arms, lighter and stiffer than the Gossamer, and it keeps the frame’s original bearing standard.

components.name: Shimano 105 FC-R7000 · 50/34 (24 mm spindle)

requires.msg: A 24 mm Hollowtech II crank needs the BB30-to-24 mm bottom bracket.

components.notes: 11-speed rings; they shift a 10-speed chain acceptably but this is outside Shimano’s chart.

upgrade.why: Shimano’s rings give the best front shifting available, and the conversion bottom bracket ends BB30 creak.

components.name: BB30 press-in bearings (6806)
components.notes: Bearing brand and condition unverified. Check for play and creak.

upgrade.why: Angular-contact bearings carry pedalling side load better than the stock radial 6806 and usually cure BB30 creak.

components.name: BB30 → Shimano 24 mm bottom bracket (Wheels Mfg)
components.notes: Threads together inside the shell, so the cups cannot walk.

upgrade.why: Lets the frame take any Shimano Hollowtech II crank.

components.name: Shimano CS-5700 · assumed 11–28
components.notes: Installed range requires tooth count (M11). On an 11-speed (HG-11) freehub a 10-speed cassette needs the 1.85 mm spacer.

components.name: Shimano Ultegra CS-6700 · 12–30
components.notes: Needs a 30T-rated rear derailleur (RD-5701-SS). On an 11-speed (HG-11) freehub a 10-speed cassette needs the 1.85 mm spacer.

upgrade.why: One easier climbing gear with tighter steps than an 11–32. Gives up the 11T, which a 50T ring rarely needs below 50 km/h.

components.name: Shimano CS-HG500-10 · 11–32
components.notes: Needs the medium-cage RD-5701-GS. On an 11-speed (HG-11) freehub a 10-speed cassette needs the 1.85 mm spacer.

upgrade.why: A 34 × 32 low gear is 12 % easier than 34 × 28. The usual answer for long or steep climbs.

components.name: Shimano CS-HG500-10 · 11–34
components.notes: Beyond every 10-speed road derailleur that this shifter can index. On an 11-speed (HG-11) freehub a 10-speed cassette needs the 1.85 mm spacer.

upgrade.why: A 1:1 low gear. Only reachable with a 9-speed mountain derailleur, which is outside Shimano’s chart.

requires.msg: Largest cog exceeds conservative RD-5700-SS 28T rating.
Required chain-wrap capacity exceeds 33T.

components.name: Shimano 105 RD-5701-SS

requires.msg: Largest cog exceeds the RD-5701-SS 30T rating.
Required chain-wrap capacity exceeds 33T (one listing says 34T).

components.notes: Same shifter pull as the installed derailleur; rated to 30T.

upgrade.why: The minimal change that makes a 12–30 cassette officially supported.

components.name: Shimano 105 RD-5701-GS (medium cage)

requires.msg: Largest cog exceeds the RD-5701-GS 32T rating.
Required chain-wrap capacity exceeds 39T (listings say 39T or 40T).

components.notes: Fit a new, longer chain with it.

upgrade.why: Opens up the 11–32 cassette with the existing shifters.

components.name: Shimano Deore RD-M592 SGS (9-speed MTB)

requires.msg: Largest cog exceeds 34T.
Capacity exceeds 45T.

components.notes: Unofficial. 9-speed Shimano mountain derailleurs share the pre-4700 road cable-pull ratio, which is why this indexes; Shimano does not list the combination.

upgrade.why: The known workaround for an 11–34 cassette on 10-speed road shifters.

components.name: Shimano Tiagra RD-4700-GS

requires.msg: Tiagra 4700 uses the 11-speed road cable-pull ratio. ST-5700 levers cannot index it.

components.notes: Listed because it looks like the obvious cheap 10-speed upgrade and is not.

components.name: Installed 10-speed chain
components.notes: Read plate markings and measure wear M11; no assumed mass.

components.name: Shimano Ultegra CN-6701 · 10-speed
components.notes: Directional: logos face outward.

upgrade.why: A worn chain wears the cassette and rings. Replace at 0.5 % elongation; this is the matching chain for 5700/6700.
Hollow pins and slotted plates, with a reusable quick link that makes hot-waxing practical.

components.name: Installed cables and housing
components.notes: Age and type unverified. ST-5700 routes both shift cables under the tape, which adds friction as they age.

upgrade.why: Under-tape shift routing is the weak point of 5700. Fresh low-friction cables and housing restore light, accurate shifting for the price of a tyre.

components.name: Shimano 105 calipers · pair
components.notes: Shimano 105 confirmed in photos; the hollow “105” logo matches the BR-5800 generation, so read the model code. Mass is the BR-5700 reference.

components.name: Shimano 105 BR-R7000 · pair
components.notes: Riders report these work with 5700 levers; Shimano’s chart does not list the pairing, so treat lever feel as unverified.

upgrade.why: Stiffer symmetric arms and rated clearance for a 28 mm tyre.

components.name: Shimano Ultegra BR-R8000 · pair
components.notes: Same lever-pairing caveat as BR-R7000.

upgrade.why: The stiffest cable rim caliper Shimano made short of Dura-Ace.

components.name: Installed brake pads

requires.msg: These pads are for alloy rims. Carbon brake tracks need carbon-specific pads.

components.notes: Compound and wear unverified.

requires.msg: BXP is an alloy-rim compound.

upgrade.why: Much stronger wet braking than stock pads and gentler on the rim. The cheapest safety upgrade here.

requires.msg: Salmon is an alloy-rim compound.

upgrade.why: The classic wet-weather compound; fits the existing cartridge holders.

components.name: SwissStop Black Prince (carbon rims)

requires.msg: Black Prince is a carbon-rim compound.

components.notes: Required with carbon brake tracks.

components.name: Installed alloy stem · 31.8 mm
components.notes: M12: length, angle, orientation and spacers. The stock part was a Cannondale C2, 6°.

components.name: Installed compact drop bar
components.notes: M12: width, reach, drop and clamp space.

components.name: Carbon compact bar (e.g. FSA K-Force Compact)
components.notes: Most carbon bars are not rated for clip-on aerobars.

upgrade.why: Damps road buzz and saves roughly 60–80 g. A comfort purchase, not a speed one.
Grippy when wet and replaces tape that has to come off anyway when the cables are changed.

components.name: Redshift Quick-Release aerobar
components.notes: Verify uncluttered clamp space beside stem and light mount.

upgrade.why: Position is most of the drag. Clip-ons are worth more on a flat solo ride than any wheelset.

components.name: Installed seatpost · diameter unverified
components.notes: M13: read marking; 27.2 mm expected, not confirmed.

upgrade.why: Two carbon leaves flex fore-aft to take the edge off rough roads; the same idea as the frame’s SAVE stays.
A clamp that holds its angle and never creaks.

components.name: Serfas · 155 mm, centre channel
components.notes: Photo: Serfas 155 with a moulded centre relief channel. Model and rail material unverified.

upgrade.why: Short-nose shape with a full cut-out, in the same 155 mm width. Saddles are personal: test before buying.

components.name: Shimano SPD-SL pedals
components.notes: Listing; read model marking.

upgrade.why: Carbon body and wider platform; keeps the same cleats.

components.name: Favero Assioma DUO power-meter pedals
components.notes: Changes the cleat system to Look Kéo.

upgrade.why: Dual-sided power moves with the rider to any bike and is independent of the BB30 crank. Makes training and every estimate in this app measurable.
Holds bottles on rough roads; available in the frame’s red.

components.name: Garmin Varia RTL515 radar tail light

upgrade.why: Rear-approach radar with a daylight-visible light. For solo road riding it is a safety upgrade ahead of any speed part.

components.name: Garmin Edge 540 on the out-front mount

upgrade.why: Shares the out-front mount with the EVO 1300 and displays the radar and power meter.

components.name: Garmin Edge 1050 · silicone case bundle
components.mass_source: Garmin claim, unit only (the case adds a few grams)
components.notes: Larger and 28 g heavier than the Edge 1040. Sits on the out-front mount above the light.

upgrade.why: The large-screen Edge: maps readable at speed, shows the radar and power meter, and its battery covers any day ride.
